Tooltip's comment offers Focusable around a span with tabIndex and a role; a real button gives the focus, the role and the press with nothing to hand-wire.

leaves.what: TooltipTrigger is controlled (isOpen, onOpenChange) with React Aria's shouldCloseOnPress={false}, and the trigger's onPress toggles it when pointerType is "touch".
leaves.why: The kit's tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus only, so on a phone a term would explain nothing; and React Aria closes a tooltip on its trigger's pointer-down and key-down (read in node_modules/react-aria's useTooltipTrigger), so a click on a term put its explanation away. Neither Tooltip's nor TooltipTrigger's comment says what a touch screen gets, nor names shouldCloseOnPress ('everything else is React Aria's').

leaves.what: focusRing() extended with the extra-small corner on the trigger; offset={8} on the Tooltip.
leaves.why: ds-build: 'The ring is `focusRing` from `<kit>/utils.ts`; extend it, do not invent another.' Tooltip: 'pass 8 for one with none, such as text'.
To learn what a press on the trigger does to an open tooltip; the first version of Term toggled on touch while React Aria was closing on pointer-down, so a second tap would have reopened it.

parts.notes: Rich tooltips (headline: the term; supporting text: its meaning) on VAT in the introduction, on terms in the cards' points and on five feature names in the table. Hover and keyboard focus are React Aria's, at the kit's timing; Escape closes. Nothing was tried in a browser or on a device. From the source: a tap shows it and a second tap hides it (pointer-down no longer closes, onPress toggles for touch alone), and the trigger losing focus hides it; whether a tap elsewhere on a touch screen takes the focus away, and so hides it, is unverified. The same term appears in several places, each with its own tooltip.

general_leaves.what: The page: a surface ground, a centred column (max-w-6xl), three labelled sections with their headings (Display stepped up from md by className, as Display's comment shows).

The first sweep of the kit printed the export and prop lines (and some style lines) of SegmentedButton, Card, Disclosure, Tooltip, Skeleton, Tag and Badge before their doc comments were found, since each file opens with its styles.
general_leaves.why: 'Doc comment first' is not the file's order: the comment sits under 60 to 300 lines of tv().

friction: Nothing was seen in a browser (none allowed), and a render-to-string smoke test was not run (my attempt wrote its script outside the project and was refused; I did not retry inside): every claim about look, dark mode and keyboard reach rests on the kit's comments and on tsc. The build was green at the first attempt, no prop was guessed wrong. What cost reads: (1) ButtonGroup's comment does not list the selection props it passes on (selectedKeys, onSelectionChange, disallowEmptySelection); one line would have saved opening the types. (2) Nothing says how to emphasise one card among several: a pricing page's commonest need. A sentence on Card ('to single one out: elevated among outlined, or …') or a variant would settle it. (3) Tooltip says nothing of touch screens: a line saying it does not open on touch, and what to do for a term in text (a ready 'term' or 'info tip' trigger, or PreviewTrigger), would have removed the one hand-made control here. (4) Card's comment does not say the root clips (overflow-hidden), which matters as soon as something inside scrolls or draws a focus ring at the edge. (5) Table has no word on a phone's width beyond an allusion to 'a box that scrolls it sideways': an example of that box, and whether a first column can stay in place, would help. (6) The doc comments sit after the styles in each file, so 'doc comment first' means scrolling past 60 to 300 lines of tv(); an index of line numbers, or the comment at the top, would make it literal. (7) TooltipTrigger closes on a press of its trigger by default; for a trigger that is text, that is the wrong default and the comment does not mention shouldCloseOnPress.
